sentences.text: Suevoleviathan was an extinct genus of primitive ichthyosaur discovered in the Early Jurassic of Holzmaden, Germany.
This large ichthyosaur measured approximately 4 meters in length.
It was unique among ichthyosaurs for retaining relatively large forefins, unlike others that showed a trend toward smaller forefins.
The genus Suevoleviathan was named in 1998 by Michael Maisch based on fossils found in the Toarcian-age Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden.
The generic name Suevoleviathan means "Swabian Leviathan".

Maisch treated S. integer as a valid species but considered it a metaspecies because its holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was incomplete and lacked important characters for specific assignment.
Suevoleviathan lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 174.7 million years ago.
